text: Lesson 3 scoped this template to exactly two resources: a logical server, and a database that lives inside it. Let's write the actual Bicep resource blocks for both.

The sqlServer resource is the administrative boundary — it holds the admin login and password that gate access to everything underneath it. This matches the real resource type Microsoft.Sql/servers, declared with its location and properties.

The sqlDatabase resource declares parent colon sqlServer, making it a true child resource of that server, matching the real Azure hierarchy. That one line also tells Bicep the correct deployment order automatically — the database can't exist before the server, and Bicep figures that out on its own, with no separate dependsOn line. Its sku — S0, Standard tier — picks a real, modest service tier appropriate for Overlook's current scale.

This version of the template is deliberately incomplete — no firewall rules yet, and the admin password is just a bare reference. Next lesson closes that password gap properly with a secure parameter, and parameterizes the whole template for dev and prod environments.
